User story: As the build engineer, I produce a read-only verification report of what already exists for platform configuration before anything is changed.
Acceptance criteria: Inspect governance docs (AGENTS.md, PROGRESS.md, NEXT_TASK.md, COMPLETION_REPORT.md, agreement file), existing config/policy code, migrations, DEV schema and RLS, permission catalogue, IAM client, shared-audit contract, gateway routes, consuming-service clients and tests; for every blueprint item mark REUSE / MOVE / NEW; reconcile these stories with IADM_Architecture_Design.md v2.0 and legacy ADM-01 configuration stories and record traceability; zero database writes; owner reviews report before S1 starts

User story: As the build engineer, I set up IADM-02 as its own service with its own gateway prefix and a health check.
Acceptance criteria: Separate service, not logic inside the existing admin monolith; proposed prefix /api/v1/iadm/02 verified for no clash with legacy /api/v1/admin; existing configuration code is moved, not copied; port assigned at build time and recorded; service starts and health check passes in DEV; no Kafka dependency

User story: As the build engineer, I map every IADM-02 capability to an exact existing permission key (or a proposed new key for owner approval) and confirm role ceilings.
Acceptance criteria: Every capability in blueprint section 8 mapped to a verified key or marked NEW - owner approval required; ceilings for R01 Super Admin, R02 System Admin, R03 Institution Admin, R04 College Admin, R28 Auditor checked against RBAC Matrix v3.0; code checks permission keys never role names; missing, expired or ambiguous authority is denied
Open decision (IADM-02 list): D3 - exact role ceilings (read, draft, approve, publish)

User story: As the build engineer, I make sure every change is durably audited, or it is not reported as a success.
Acceptance criteria: Shared audit client verified; one verified mechanism chosen (same transaction or approved outbox); test proves that if audit is unavailable the change is not reported as successful; no local duplicate audit store; each record holds actor, action, resource, before/after reference, reason, correlation ID, timestamp
Open decision (IADM-02 list): D9 - atomicity between publication and audit

User story: As the build engineer, I reuse existing configuration storage and isolate drafts from consumers.
Acceptance criteria: Existing tables reused where present; gaps listed as proposals only - no new table, migration, RLS policy or grant without owner approval; draft and unpublished values invisible to consumers and unauthorized actors (Java checks plus RLS); institute remains the isolation boundary for any institute-scoped row
Open decision (IADM-02 list): D6 - table names, RLS, version storage

User story: As the build engineer, I make create-draft, decision, publish and rollback safe to retry.
Acceptance criteria: Each of these operations accepts an idempotency key and correlation ID; same key returns the same result; no duplicate drafts, decisions, versions or audit entries; retry resumes at the failed step
Blueprint trace: Section 6 API rules; section 9 failure branches

User story: As the build engineer, I prepare DEV-only demo data so that administrators have real configuration to work on.
Acceptance criteria: Seed through an approved DEV-only procedure; personas R01 Super Admin (two separate people so one drafts and another approves), R02, R03, R04, R28; one approved service identity; illustrative keys CFG-PLATFORM-001 and 002; VER-001 initial published version; DRAFT-001 valid and DRAFT-002 invalid; seed is re-runnable; nothing touches production; key names approved by owner first
Done level required: Demo-verified (personas can log in, data visible)
Open decision (IADM-02 list): D1 - initial list of configuration keys

Actor (role code and name): R01 Super Admin (also R02 System Admin within ceiling)
User story: As an authorized operator, I can view and search the platform configuration catalogue by domain, key, status, owner and version.
Acceptance criteria: Catalogue shows real keys (not an empty list); search and filters work; states handled: loading, empty, filtered, not found, error, unauthorized; read-only

User story: As an authorized operator, I can inspect a key's type, owner, constraints, consumers, active value and history.
Acceptance criteria: Detail screen shows all of these; deprecated and missing-dependency states shown; read-only

User story: As an authorized operator, I see a dashboard of the active version, pending drafts, recent publications and validation failures.
Acceptance criteria: Dashboard loads real counts and lists; partial dependency failure shown without hiding the rest; unauthorized state handled
Blueprint trace: Section 5A (screen only, no story ID in blueprint)

User story: As an authorized operator, I can create a configuration draft with a reason.
Acceptance criteria: Reason is mandatory; unknown key rejected with 'not registered' message; draft status and ID shown; audit entry written; idempotent; unauthorized denied

User story: As an authorized operator, I can edit a draft that is not yet published.
Acceptance criteria: Only unpublished drafts editable; concurrent edit conflict detected and shown; published versions never editable; audit entry written

User story: As an authorized operator, I can validate a draft before approval.
Acceptance criteria: Checks type, allowed values, cross-key rules and compatibility; invalid draft cannot be approved or published; field-level errors shown; correct and revalidate works; DRAFT-002 fails and DRAFT-001 passes in demo

User story: As R01, I can view the policy catalogue and propose a change to a policy definition as a draft.
Acceptance criteria: Policies listed read-only for others; policy change follows the same draft, validate, approve, publish path; version conflict shown; audit entry written
Blueprint trace: Section 5A policy catalogue; section 6 (no story ID in blueprint)

User story: As R02, I can only do the technical actions my ceiling allows and cannot approve business policy or publish restricted defaults.
Acceptance criteria: Allowed actions follow the decided ceiling; approve, restricted publish and role-grant attempts denied with clear message; negative test passes
Audit event (proposed name): None for denial; audit for any allowed mutation

User story: As an authorized operator, I can submit a validated draft for decision when policy requires approval.
Acceptance criteria: Only validated drafts can be submitted; status becomes PENDING_APPROVAL; unvalidated draft rejected; approval-required rule follows owner decision. NOTE: the blueprint API table has no submit endpoint, so the endpoint is TBC

User story: As an authorized approver, I can approve or reject a draft with a reason.
Acceptance criteria: Reason recorded; person who wrote the draft cannot approve it (denied until the owner decides otherwise); pending, approved, rejected, expired and unauthorized states shown; audit entry written
Open decision (IADM-02 list): D4, D5 - same person drafting and approving

User story: As an authorized publisher, I can publish an approved version with an effective time and release notes.
Acceptance criteria: Success shown only after the version is active and audit is durable; failed publish keeps the approved draft and shows 'not published'; new active version visible in catalogue

User story: As R01, I can see version history and compare the active version with a prior one.
Acceptance criteria: Version list and detail with who, when, why; side-by-side comparison; published history is immutable

User story: As an authorized operator, I can safely retry a failed draft, approval or publication step.
Acceptance criteria: Approval service down keeps draft pending; database failure shows no false success; publish failure preserves approved draft; retry creates no duplicate drafts, decisions, versions or audit entries
Permission (plain meaning; exact key TBC: Same as the step being retried
Audit event (proposed name): Same as the step being retried

User story: As the build engineer, I let consuming services authenticate with their own service identity and limit them to approved domains and keys.
Acceptance criteria: Identity comes from authenticated credentials, never from a caller-supplied consumer ID alone; permitted domains/keys and validity per consumer; reuse existing IAM authority, no duplicate identity registry; R27 API Client stays out

User story: As an approved service, I can read only my authorized effective configuration.
Acceptance criteria: Returns effective approved values, version, schema metadata and freshness timestamp; only authorized domains and keys returned

User story: As an approved service, I am denied keys outside my domain and I never see drafts or unapproved values.
Acceptance criteria: Denied-domain test passes; draft and unapproved values never returned; read contract cannot be used to change configuration

User story: As a consumer, I can detect version, freshness and unavailable states.
Acceptance criteria: Stale and unavailable states returned explicitly; consumer uses last-known-good only if an approved rule exists, otherwise fails closed; no invented default values; outage simulation shown in demo

User story: As an operator, I can see in a read-only diagnostic view which consumers last fetched which version and which are stale.
Acceptance criteria: Shows last successful fetch, active version and stale/unavailable status per consumer; no edit actions
Permission (plain meaning; exact key TBC: View configuration catalogue (or diagnostics key TBC)

User story: As IADM-01, I can read the platform defaults and policy needed for institute onboarding without storing my own copy.
Acceptance criteria: Reads through the IADM-02 contract; fails closed where a policy is mandatory; no invented defaults; no duplicate default store in IADM-01; S0 report shows how IADM-01 gets defaults today

User story: As an authorized operator, I can publish a corrective version based on a prior version when a bad publication needs fixing.
Acceptance criteria: Preview of prior version; guarded by approval and authority; result is a new immutable version that references the prior one; history is not erased; consumers pick it up by pull; audit links to the earlier publication and reason
Open decision (IADM-02 list): D11 - new version vs pointer change

User story: As R28, I can view permitted configuration history read-only.
Acceptance criteria: History and versions visible within assigned scope; every mutation, approval, publish and rollback attempt denied with 'Auditor access is read-only'

Actor (role code and name): R03 Institution Admin, R04 College Admin
User story: As R03 or R04, I cannot change platform defaults or policy.
Acceptance criteria: Write, approve, publish and rollback denied for both; R03 sees read or consume access only if RBAC Matrix v3.0 explicitly allows it; R04 has no IADM-02 admin access; checked on both API and screens

User story: As an operator, I get a non-blocking notification status when COM (notifications) is unavailable.
Acceptance criteria: Main workflow completes; notification shown as delayed; independent retry; no Kafka
Open decision (IADM-02 list): D12 - which changes notify, pull or signal

User story: As R03, I can request an institute-level override of a platform default, and R01 can approve it.
Acceptance criteria: PARKED. Only after the owner approves overrides, which keys may be overridden, the precedence model and the RLS design; until then no override exists and platform defaults only apply
Permission (plain meaning; exact key TBC: Request configuration override (does not exist unless approved)
Blueprint trace: Not in blueprint Markdown; appears only in the PNG

User story: As the build engineer, I run the full working demo and record the evidence.
Acceptance criteria: Run the demo checklist (section 15) end to end; record screenshots or video, API test report, audit evidence, version IDs and correlation IDs; verify no direct frontend database access, no cross-institute leakage, no duplicate settings store; update progress docs; show 'RBAC v3.0 Compliant' only when every check is verified in code, gateway, catalogue, DEV schema, tests and demo
Blueprint trace: Section 15; Part C; Part D Phase 5
